name.text: Evaluating the Convergence and Value of an exponetial Improper Integral

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the integral below and determine if it converges or diverges.

Note: \( \infty\) is entered as inf \( -\infty\) is entered as minf and \( e\) is entered as %e.

\(\displaystyle \int_{{@lower_lm@}}^{{@upper_lm@}} {@num*%e@}^{ \displaystyle {@(-x^power/den)@}} \,dx=\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

Therefore, the integral is [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Recall that we can’t evaluate the integral as long as there is an infinity in one of the limits. Therefore, we’ll need to replace infinity with a parameter \( t \) as follows:

The given improper integral is

\(\displaystyle I = \int_{@lower_lm@}^{@upper_lm@} {@fx@} \, dx. \)

We will first evaluate whether the integral converges or diverges by finding the limit of the integral as \( t \to \infty \):

\(\displaystyle I = \int_{@lower_lm@}^{t} {@fx@} \, dx. \)

The antiderivative of \(\displaystyle {@fx@} \) is:

\(\displaystyle \int {@fx@} \, dx = {@indef_int@} \)

Now, evaluate the integral from \( {@lower_lm@} \) to \( t \):

\(\displaystyle I(t) = \left[ {@indef_int@} \right]_{@lower_lm@}^t = {@indef_val@} \)

Take the limit as \( t \to \infty \):

\(\displaystyle I = \lim_{t \to \infty} \left( {@indef_val@} \right) = {@def_integral@} \)

The improper integral is {@mcq_correct(ta_4)[1]@}, and its exact value is \( \boxed{{@def_integral@}} \).
